name: hardening-readonly
title: Exposed-host hardening PR A: default-deny read-command classification, --read-only host mode, denial error code (protocol 1.11.0)
issue: Approved by the user 2026-10-13 (design and decisions: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/exposed-host-hardening.md, sections 1, 2c, 3, 4 and the Decisions block; read it first). Decisions that apply: viewers are strictly read-only and may NOT enter play mode; a denial gets a new ERROR CODE (not a message prefix), which means a minor protocol bump 1.10.0 -> 1.11.0; the pre-auth accept thread and proxy support are out of scope. Scope (PR A, useful alone, no auth change): (1) editor-server/src/EditorServer.cpp: add `IsReadCommand`, an ALLOW list with default deny (seed from IsPolledCommand ~l.1971, mostly reads, plus GetCurrentScene, GetOpenScene, GetProjectInfo, GetPlayState; review every protocol.json command and classify it explicitly as read / write / admin; commands that can execute scripts or change anything, including SendInput, WritePlaySnapshot, EnterPlayMode/play-mode commands, Shutdown, RescanAssets, Undo/Redo, Save*, import settings, are NOT read). Do not reuse IsEditOnlyCommand (it only lists 13 file-writing commands and runs only in play mode). (2) a host option `--read-only` (HostOptions.cpp + docs): the gate sits beside the existing _playMode check (~l.2114) and refuses every non-read command with the denial error; it works with the legacy --token-env token and with no token. (3) the denial error code: add an optional trailing `code` to the Error message (or the closest equivalent in protocol.json; find how Error is declared, keep old clients working through a trailing field), define stable codes (`readOnly`, `forbidden`), bump protocol minor to 1.11.0, regenerate every generated client and the golden vectors with the generators in editor-server/protocol/generators (cpp, csharp, typescript, test_vectors), commit the regenerated files; the `protocol` CI job must stay green. ServerInfo gains NOTHING in this PR except what is needed to say the host is read-only: add a trailing `readOnly` bool to ServerInfo only if cheap and backwards compatible, otherwise leave it for the per-user-tokens PR and say so. (4) Tests (socket/unit, run on every leg incl. Linux): an EXHAUSTIVE classification test that iterates every command id in protocol.json and requires an explicit class so a new command cannot ship unclassified (fail with the command name); with --read-only every write command is refused with the right code and the connection stays usable, every read command still works, Shutdown is refused; Hello/ping/health keep working; play-mode behaviour unchanged. (5) Docs: docs/editor.html and docs/logging-and-editor.html (the --read-only option, the classification, the denial code, the protocol 1.11.0 entry in the protocol history/changelog place the docs use), deploy docs mention if relevant. Do not touch the frontend repo (a later item syncs it). DECISION UPDATE (user, 2026-10-13, after the first attempt stopped on this): the Error payload is raw UTF-8 message bytes with no length prefix, so DO NOT append a trailing code to Error. Use a NEW response message `ErrorCoded` (message + code) and keep Error unchanged. A host sends ErrorCoded only to clients that declare support in Hello through a new TRAILING Hello capability flag (add it as an optional trailing field with a default of false so old clients, which never send it, keep working); a client without the flag keeps getting the plain Error with a readable message such as `read-only host: <command> is not allowed` so older clients still see why. Add the new response id in protocol.json (next free id in the right range), bump the minor protocol version to 1.11.0, regenerate all generated clients and golden vectors, document the capability negotiation and the codes (readOnly, forbidden) in docs/logging-and-editor.html, and test both paths (new client gets ErrorCoded with the right code; legacy client gets Error). A previous attempt left a malformed ledger/hardening-readonly/dev.json (a stray backslash sequence): overwrite it with valid JSON when you finish. If a worktree for this item already exists (ledger/hardening-readonly/state.json), reuse it instead of creating another.
